caption: HazeChain: satellite-verified peat fire evidence and pay-for-no-fire escrow
text: This is HazeChain, built for the IEEE ClimateChain Global Hackathon, in the Climate Data and Environmental Monitoring track.

caption: 58,466 NASA fire detections in Central Kalimantan, 17 to 24 October 2026
text: This is Central Kalimantan, this week. Between the seventeenth and the twenty-fourth of October, NASA satellites recorded fifty-eight thousand fire detections in this one area. Seventy-nine percent of them are on drained peat, which releases about eight hundred tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent for every hectare that burns. This smoke is the haze over Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore right now.

caption: The gap: contested attribution, and no trusted way to pay for fire-free land
text: Satellites already see every fire. What fails is what happens next. Attribution is contested, because fires cross boundaries and evidence can be disputed. And communities that keep their land from burning are rarely paid for it, because a funder has to trust somebody's paperwork.

caption: AI: cluster pixels into fires, find the ignition, decide started inside vs spread in
text: HazeChain's AI clusters the raw pixels into fire events and finds where each one started. Here, a fire started inside an oil palm concession, and the attribution confidence is above our threshold of point seven. For every area a fire touches, the model asks one question: did it start here, or spread in from outside? Only starts count. Fires already burning when the record began get half confidence, because their true start is unknown.

caption: 152 of 260 concessions stayed fire-free: the land managers a fund should pay
text: This concession, ninety-nine percent peat, had zero fire pixels all week. One hundred and fifty-two of the two hundred and sixty concessions here stayed fire-free. Those are the land managers a climate fund should be paying.

caption: 7-day fire risk, LightGBM: ROC-AUC 0.83 vs 0.68 baseline on the unseen 2025 season
text: A gradient boosted model trained on seven years of fire seasons forecasts next week's risk for every five kilometre cell. On the 2025 season, which it never saw, it scores an area under the curve of point eight three, against point six eight for the naive baseline. It also beats the baseline in the El Niño year of 2023.

caption: Every day's evidence is a Merkle root, written once to Ethereum Sepolia
text: Now the part a regulator or a court cares about. Every day, each detection, fire event and attribution is hashed into one Merkle root, written to Ethereum once, and never again. The browser has just downloaded twenty-three thousand rows of evidence, rebuilt the root itself, and it is identical to the root stored on Sepolia. Asking the contract whether this attribution row is part of the record: proven.

caption: Change one value and the contract rejects it
text: Now the confidence is changed, the way someone might try after a fire. The contract rejects it. Nobody, including us, can quietly edit this evidence.

caption: Pay-for-no-fire escrow: paid, slashed, or disputed, every step on-chain
text: This is where the money moves. A funder locks money against one area for a fire season. When it ends, the oracle reports ignitions, citing a day of anchored evidence. This village and this concession stayed fire-free, so they were paid automatically. This concession had five confident ignitions, so its pledge was slashed to a fire suppression pool. And this one had a borderline attribution of point seven one, so the company disputed with field evidence, and settlement is frozen until an arbiter rules. Every step is a real transaction on Sepolia, and the contract source is verified.

caption: Under US$0.04 per tonne of CO2e: trustworthy, results-based climate finance
text: A fire-free village programme in Riau reported a ninety percent drop in burnt area, for about thirty thousand dollars a village. Keep just one thousand hectares of peat from burning, and that is under four cents per tonne of carbon dioxide. HazeChain makes that kind of payment trustworthy enough for governments, commodity buyers and climate funds, and the same open pipeline works on every peatland on Earth. Ahead of COP thirty-one, this is transparent, results-based climate finance. Thank you.
